Definition: from a derivative of G3541; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid:--dull, slothful.
BiblicalUsage: Dull and slothful are the two faces of the same word: dull of hearing, and slothful in following. The Hebrews are dull of hearing, so the deep things are hard to utter; and they are told not to be slothful, but followers of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dull hearing makes a slothful life: the ears that will not listen soon stop following, and the promises go to the patient.
